cards.name: Patch Tool
cards.summary: Repairs an area by dragging a selection: you outline the flaw (or a clean patch) and drag it, and Photoshop fills the selected area with texture from the drop location while blending it into the surrounding colour and light, so the seam disappears. In Content-Aware mode the fill is synthesised from the surroundings instead of copied straight across.
cards.how: Pick it from the Spot Healing Brush flyout (J; the harvested J cycle runs Spot Healing Brush, Healing Brush, Patch, Content-Aware Move, Red Eye). Draw a freehand outline around the flaw (the tool draws selections like the Lasso) or start from any existing selection, then drag the selection onto clean texture and release. Options bar: Normal or Content-Aware patch (harvest key contentAware); Source / Destination decides whether the selection is the area to repair or the patch to copy (harvest key healingDirection read back only healFromDest2Src); Transparent (transparency) blends texture only; Use Pattern (pattern) fills from a pattern. In Content-Aware mode Structure (patchStructureAdapt, read back 4) sets how strictly existing structure is kept and Color (patchColorAdaptation, read back 0) how much colour is blended; Sample All Layers (sampleAllLayers) lets it repair onto an empty layer. Diffusion (healSmoothFactor, read back 5) sets how fast the patch blends into its edge.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "patchSelection" (harvest invoke). The drag itself cannot be scripted. Closest scripted result: select the flaw with Selection.select (ps_api Selection), then run Edit/Content-Aware Fill (ps_menu 1510) by its harvested event, executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("cafWorkspace"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO), which in the harvest's live test filled the selection onto a new layer without opening the workspace. Edit/Fill (ps_menu 1042) also runs silently through its harvested event fill, but the recorded descriptor fills with the foreground colour; the Content-Aware contents value is not in this harvest. app.runMenuItem with these numeric menu ids is refused (harvest audit), so use the events.
use_for: removing a stray object or person from grass, sand, sky or a plain wall
cleaning larger skin flaws, scars and wrinkles in a portrait retouch
erasing a logo or print from a T-shirt or packaging in a mockup
hiding seams and dust marks in a scanned background texture
avoid: next to hard, high-contrast edges: the healing blend pulls the edge colour into the patch; use the Clone Stamp Tool there
for small spots: the Spot Healing Brush Tool is faster
for large removals on busy backgrounds: the Remove Tool or Edit > Generative Fill usually gives a cleaner fill
Normal mode on an empty layer: it repairs the active layer's pixels only

review.changes: script_api: dropped the claim that runMenuItem(1042) opens the Fill dialog (the harvest audit says runMenuItem refuses these menu ids, and the harvested Fill descriptor is a foreground-colour fill); the scripted route is now Content-Aware Fill through its verified cafWorkspace event under DialogModes.NO.

cards.name: Path Selection Tool
cards.summary: Selects whole paths: every anchor of a path component on a shape layer, work path, saved path or vector mask, so you can move, duplicate, transform, align or combine the component as one piece without touching individual points.
cards.how: Press A (Shift+A toggles with the Direct Selection Tool, per the harvested cycle). Click a path to select the whole component, Shift-click or drag a marquee to add more, Alt-drag to duplicate, Ctrl+T to transform. The options bar's path operations (harvest key shapeOperation: add, subtract, intersect, exclude overlap) set how the selected components combine, and the align / distribute buttons line components up. The harvest also reads back a boolean 'Pbbx' that is probably the Show Transform Controls checkbox; that mapping is not confirmed.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "pathComponentSelectTool" (harvest invoke). Instead of clicking, a script reaches paths through Document.pathItems (ps_api PathItems / PathItem): PathItem.select, deselect, duplicate, remove, makeSelection, fillPath, strokePath, makeClippingPath. PathItem has no translate member in the harvest, so moving or transforming a component by script needs an Action Manager descriptor this harvest does not record.
use_for: repositioning or duplicating a logo shape inside a shape layer
combining or cutting shape components with path operations to build an icon
aligning several shape components on a banner layout
selecting a vector mask path to move or scale it
avoid: editing single anchor points or handles: use the Direct Selection Tool
moving pixel layers or whole layers: use the Move Tool
complex vector construction: draw it in Illustrator and paste as a shape layer

cards.name: Pattern Stamp Tool
cards.summary: A brush that paints with a chosen pattern instead of a colour. With Aligned on, the pattern stays in register across separate strokes so it reads as one continuous tile; with Impressionist on, the pattern is smeared into loose paint dabs.
cards.how: Press S (Shift+S toggles with the Clone Stamp Tool). Pick a pattern from the options bar's pattern picker (harvest key pattern), set brush size and hardness, blend Mode, Opacity and Flow, and paint on a layer. Aligned keeps the tile continuous between strokes (the harvested boolean 'StmA', read back true, is probably Aligned; not confirmed); Impressionist (impressionist) gives a painterly smear. All Brush Settings dynamics (texture, dual brush, scatter, smoothing) apply as with the Brush Tool.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "patternStampTool" (harvest invoke). A stroke can be scripted by building a path (PathItems.add) and calling PathItem.strokePath with ToolType.PATTERNSTAMP (ps_api ToolType value 6); it uses the tool's current pattern and brush, which must be set beforehand. strokePath's second argument, simulatePressure, fakes a pressure taper; real tablet pressure and freehand variation are not reproduced.
use_for: painting fabric, paper or brick texture into selected parts of a mockup
hand-filling irregular areas with a seamless pattern
painterly textured backgrounds with Impressionist on
avoid: filling a whole area evenly: use a Pattern fill layer (Layer/New Fill Layer/Pattern) or the Pattern Overlay layer style, which stay editable
copying image content from another spot: use the Clone Stamp Tool
painting straight onto the photo layer: paint on an empty layer so the strokes can be undone or masked

review.changes: script_api: the harvested PathItem.strokePath(tool, simulatePressure) has a simulatePressure flag, so "pressure is not reproduced" now says a taper can be simulated.

cards.name: Pen Tool
cards.summary: Draws precise Bezier paths: a click sets a corner point, a click-and-drag sets a smooth point with handles. The result is a path (work path, saved path or vector mask) or a shape layer, used for clean cut-outs, selections, vector masks and custom shapes.
cards.how: Press P (Shift+P toggles with the Freeform Pen Tool). Choose Shape or Path in the options bar (harvest key geometryToolMode, read back path) and the path operation (shapeOperation). Click for corner points, drag for curves, Alt-drag a handle to break it into a cusp, hold Ctrl to switch temporarily to direct selection, and click the first point to close. With Auto Add/Delete on (probably the harvested boolean 'AAdd', read back true) clicking a segment adds a point and clicking a point removes it. Then Ctrl+Enter makes a selection from the path, or use it as a vector mask.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "penTool" (harvest invoke). The tool's output is fully scriptable: Document.pathItems.add (ps_api PathItems.add) builds a path from SubPathInfo / PathPointInfo with exact anchors and handles, then PathItem.makeSelection, fillPath, strokePath or makeClippingPath use it. Turning that path into a live shape layer needs an Action Manager descriptor this harvest does not record.
use_for: hard-edged product cut-outs (bottles, packaging, cars, electronics)
vector masks that stay sharp when the layer is scaled
clipping paths for print catalogues
drawing a custom icon or logo shape inside a Photoshop layout
avoid: hair, fur and soft edges: use Select and Mask or the Object Selection Tool
a rough, quick selection: the Lasso or Polygonal Lasso Tool is faster
full vector illustration or logo artwork for print: draw it in Illustrator

cards.name: Pencil Tool
cards.summary: Paints hard-edged strokes in the foreground colour with no anti-aliasing: every pixel is either fully painted or untouched, so a 1 px pencil gives crisp stair-stepped lines. It is the pixel-art and hard-mask counterpart of the Brush Tool.
cards.how: Press B (Shift+B cycles Brush, Pencil, Color Replacement, Mixer Brush). Set the size (1 px for pixel art), Mode and Opacity, then click or drag; Shift-click draws a straight line from the last point. Auto Erase (probably the harvested boolean 'PncA', read back false) paints the background colour when a stroke starts on foreground-coloured pixels. Brush Settings dynamics and smoothing (harvest smoothing / smoothingValue) apply as with the Brush Tool; zoom in with the pixel grid for sprite work.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "pencilTool" (harvest invoke). A stroke can be scripted by building a path (PathItems.add) and calling PathItem.strokePath with ToolType.PENCIL (ps_api ToolType value 1), using the tool's current size and the foreground colour; single pixels can also be set by selecting a 1 px square with Selection.select and calling Selection.fill. strokePath's simulatePressure argument fakes a pressure taper; real tablet pressure is not reproduced.
use_for: pixel art, game sprites and 8-bit icons
1 px rules and guides in a UI mockup
hard-edged touch-ups on a layer mask where no soft edge is wanted
favicon and small-icon pixel fixes
avoid: smooth illustration or high-resolution artwork: edges look jagged; use the Brush Tool
clean straight vector lines that must stay editable: use the Line Tool or Pen Tool
on an anti-aliased image you want to keep smooth: pencil edges stand out against it

review.changes: script_api: noted the harvested strokePath simulatePressure argument instead of saying pressure cannot be reproduced.

cards.name: Perspective Crop Tool
cards.summary: Crops and un-distorts in one step: you place the four corners of the crop on a plane that is skewed in the photo (a document, sign, screen, facade) and on commit Photoshop crops to it and stretches it into a straight-on rectangle.
cards.how: Press C (the harvested C cycle runs Crop, Perspective Crop, Slice, Slice Select). Click the four corners of the plane, or drag a box and move each corner onto the plane's edges, using the grid to line up with straight lines in the image, then press Enter. Width, Height and Resolution in the options bar force the output size; the harvest reads all options back as one object 'PCrO' (class 'PcOC') without breaking out its fields.
cards.script_api: Only the tool can be selected: app.currentTool = "perspectiveCropTool" (harvest invoke). This harvest records no event that applies a perspective crop. Edit/Transform/Perspective (ps_menu 2203) is also interactive, and Image/Crop (ps_menu 1044) crops to a selection without correcting perspective.
use_for: turning a phone photo of a poster, menu or whiteboard into a flat, scan-like image
extracting a facade or sign texture as a straight-on rectangle for a mockup
correcting keystone in an architecture shot when a crop is acceptable
avoid: when the full canvas must be kept: use Edit/Transform/Perspective or Edit/Perspective Warp
for lens barrel or pincushion distortion: use the Lens Correction filter
on strongly angled planes: the stretched far side goes soft; reshoot straighter if you can

cards.name: Polygon Tool
cards.summary: Draws regular polygons as live shapes, by default on a shape layer. The number of sides (harvest sides, read back 5), the star ratio (starRatio, 100% = plain polygon, lower values push the sides inward into a star) and a corner radius for rounded points stay editable afterwards.
cards.how: Press U (the harvested U cycle runs Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Line, Custom Shape; the Rounded Rectangle entry is a leftover in the shortcut file, since app.currentTool rejects 'roundedRectangleTool'). Set the number of sides and the corner radius in the options bar, drag on the canvas (Shift keeps proportions), or click once to type exact width, height, sides, corner radius and star ratio. Edit the live shape later in the Properties panel. Fill and stroke come from the options bar; linkCornerRadius keeps all corner radii equal.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "polygonTool" (harvest invoke). A script can build the same outline from computed vertices with Document.pathItems.add (ps_api PathItems.add) and then fillPath, strokePath or makeSelection; a live polygon shape layer with editable sides and star ratio needs an Action Manager descriptor this harvest does not record.
use_for: hexagon badges and icon backgrounds
star bursts for sale stickers and price tags (star ratio below 100%)
triangles for play buttons and arrows
geometric pattern elements and rounded polygon photo frames
avoid: irregular shapes: draw them with the Pen Tool
Pixels mode when the shape may change later: it loses the live shape
complex vector artwork destined for print: build it in Illustrator

equivalents.AI: Adobe Shape Construction Regular Polygon Tool

review.changes: how: flagged the Rounded Rectangle Tool in the harvested U cycle as a kys leftover (the harvest shows app.currentTool rejects it).

cards.name: Polygonal Lasso Tool
cards.summary: Makes a straight-edged selection by clicking corner points: each click adds a straight segment, and the selection closes when you click the start point or double-click.
cards.how: Press L (Shift+L cycles Lasso, Polygonal Lasso, Magnetic Lasso). Click each corner; hold Shift while clicking to constrain the segment to 45 degree steps, press Backspace to remove the last point, Esc to cancel, and hold Alt to draw freehand segments temporarily. Shift / Alt before the first click add to or subtract from an existing selection. Feather and Anti-alias are on the options bar; the harvest reads them back as 'DrwR' (pixels, 0) and 'DrwA' (true), probably feather and anti-alias, not confirmed.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "polySelTool" (harvest invoke). The same straight-edged selection is made by Selection.select([[x,y], ...], SelectionType.REPLACE / EXTEND / DIMINISH / INTERSECT, feather, antiAlias) (ps_api Selection, SelectionType) from a list of corner points.
use_for: selecting buildings, boxes, windows and other straight-edged objects
selecting a phone or laptop screen to drop a design into a mockup
quick angular cut-outs and geometric masks
avoid: curved or organic edges: use the Pen Tool, Object Selection Tool or Quick Selection Tool
hair and soft edges: refine with Select and Mask
very long outlines with many corners: the Pen Tool path is easier to correct afterwards

cards.name: Quick Selection Tool
cards.summary: Selects by painting: as you brush over an area, the selection grows outward to the nearest edges it finds from colour and texture, so a few strokes select a person, product or sky with fairly clean edges.
cards.how: Press W (Shift+W cycles Quick Selection, Magic Wand, Object Selection). Brush across the object; after the first stroke the tool adds to the selection automatically, Alt-brush subtracts, [ and ] change the brush size. Options: Sample All Layers (quickSelectSampleAllLayers), Auto-Enhance (autoEnhance) for smoother edges at some speed cost, Select Subject, and Select and Mask to refine. The harvest also reads back quickSelectSpread and quickSelectStickiness (50 each) and quickSelectMode (1); what these control is not confirmed.
cards.script_api: Only the tool can be selected: app.currentTool = "quickSelectTool" (harvest invoke); brush strokes cannot be scripted. Alternatives: Select/Subject (ps_menu 1461) by its harvested event, executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("autoCutout"), desc, DialogModes.NO) with sampleAllLayers false in desc, for the main subject (app.runMenuItem refuses the numeric menu id, per the harvest audit); or Selection.select (ps_api Selection) for a known polygon.
use_for: fast first-pass selection of a product, person or sky against a contrasting background
selecting a garment or object to recolour with an adjustment layer
a base mask before refining hair in Select and Mask
avoid: hair, fur and fine detail: finish with the Refine Edge Brush Tool in Select and Mask
low-contrast edges where the selection bleeds: use the Pen Tool
a whole subject in one click: use the Object Selection Tool or Select/Subject

review.changes: script_api: Select/Subject is reached through its verified autoCutout event, not runMenuItem(1461), which the harvest audit says is refused.

cards.name: Rectangle Tool
cards.summary: Draws rectangles and rounded rectangles as live shapes, by default on a shape layer, with editable width, height, fill, stroke and corner radii (all four linked or each set separately). It also replaces the older Rounded Rectangle Tool.
cards.how: Press U (the harvested U cycle runs Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Line, Custom Shape; the Rounded Rectangle entry is a leftover in the shortcut file, since app.currentTool rejects 'roundedRectangleTool'). Drag on the canvas: Shift makes a square, Alt draws from the centre. Set fill and stroke in the options bar and the corner radius in its radius field (harvest key radius, read back 12; the harvest labels it 'Feather Radius' after the shared terminology key, but on this tool it is most likely the corner radius). Drag the on-canvas corner widgets or use the Properties panel for exact size, position and per-corner radii (radii, linked by rectangleRadiiLinked). The Shape / Path / Pixels picker is harvest key geometryToolMode (read back shape).
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "rectangleTool" (harvest invoke). A script can draw the outline with Document.pathItems.add (ps_api PathItems.add) and fill it with PathItem.fillPath, or make a rectangular Selection.select and Selection.fill for pixels; a live rectangle shape layer with editable corner radii needs an Action Manager descriptor this harvest does not record.
use_for: UI cards, buttons and app screens in a mockup
text plates and colour blocks behind a poster or thumbnail headline
rounded photo placeholders and frames in a social post layout
banner and flyer layout blocks
avoid: Pixels mode when the shape may change: it is not editable afterwards
print-ready logo or vector artwork: build it in Illustrator
a rectangular selection for editing pixels: use the Rectangular Marquee Tool

review.changes: how: flagged the Rounded Rectangle entry of the U cycle as a kys leftover that app.currentTool rejects (backs the summary's "replaces" claim); geometryToolMode now quotes the harvested value (shape) instead of implying Path / Pixels are harvested enum values.

cards.name: Rectangular Marquee Tool
cards.summary: Drags out a rectangular selection, the basic way to isolate a rectangle of pixels for cropping, filling, copying or masking an adjustment.
cards.how: Press M (Shift+M toggles with the Elliptical Marquee Tool). Drag a box; Shift constrains to a square, Alt draws from the centre, holding Space while dragging moves the box. Shift / Alt / Shift+Alt before dragging add, subtract or intersect. The options bar has Feather, Style (Normal, Fixed Ratio, Fixed Size) for exact pixel boxes, and an Anti-alias box that is greyed out for this tool (it is live on the Elliptical Marquee); the harvest reads these back as 'MrqF' (pixels, 0), 'MrqA' (false) and the object 'MrqI' (class 'MrqC'), a probable but unconfirmed mapping.
cards.script_api: Selecting the tool: app.currentTool = "marqueeRectTool" (harvest invoke). The same selection is made by Selection.select([[l,t],[r,t],[r,b],[l,b]], SelectionType.REPLACE / EXTEND / DIMINISH / INTERSECT, feather, antiAlias) (ps_api Selection, SelectionType); follow with Selection.fill / copy, or Image/Crop (ps_menu 1044) to crop to it.
use_for: selecting an exact area to crop, copy or fill
a fixed-size selection for a banner or thumbnail crop
masking an adjustment layer to a rectangular band
selecting a block to clear or recolour in a layout
avoid: non-rectangular areas: use the Polygonal Lasso Tool or Elliptical Marquee Tool
a rectangle that is a design element: draw it with the Rectangle Tool so it stays editable
soft vignettes: feather the selection or use a gradient mask instead of a hard box

review.changes: how: Anti-alias is shown but greyed out on the Rectangular Marquee options bar; said so instead of implying it is a working option.

cards.name: Red Eye Tool
cards.summary: Fixes flash red-eye with a click: Photoshop finds the red pupil around the click point and replaces it with a dark, neutral pupil.
cards.how: Press J (the harvested J cycle runs Spot Healing Brush, Healing Brush, Patch, Content-Aware Move, Red Eye). Zoom in and click each red pupil, or drag a box around the eye. The options bar has Pupil Size and Darken Amount; the harvest reads back radius (labelled 'Feather Radius' after the shared terminology key, value 50) and darken (50), most likely Pupil Size and Darken Amount. Raise Pupil Size if a red ring remains and Darken Amount for a deeper pupil. It edits the active pixel layer, so work on a duplicate.
cards.script_api: Only the tool can be selected: app.currentTool = "redEyeTool" (harvest invoke); the click cannot be scripted and this harvest records no red-eye event.
use_for: fixing red-eye in flash portraits and event photos
quick batch clean-up of party or wedding snapshots before a layout
avoid: pet eye-shine (green, yellow or white): the tool targets red; paint a dark pupil on a new layer instead
pupils that are not red: it has nothing to detect
high-end portrait retouching: a hand-painted pupil with catchlight preserved looks more natural

cards.name: Refine Edge Brush Tool
cards.id: taskspace/Select and Mask/Refine Edge Brush Tool
cards.summary: A brush that exists only inside the Select and Mask workspace: brushing along hair, fur or other fuzzy edges makes Photoshop re-analyse that edge zone, pulling fine strands into the selection and dropping the background between them.
cards.how: Make a rough selection, open Select/Select and Mask, then press R (the harvested shortcut inside that workspace) or pick the tool from the workspace's toolbar. Brush along the edge so the stroke covers both hair and background; Alt-brush to undo areas. Check the result with View: Overlay or On Black, turn on Decontaminate Colors if colour fringes remain, and output to a layer mask.
cards.script_api: None: the harvest found no id app.currentTool accepts outside the workspace ('selectionLabRefineTool' raised a General Photoshop error). Select/Select and Mask (ps_menu 1115) runs through its harvested event, executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("refineSelectionEdge"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO), which in the harvest's live test applied default settings without opening the workspace (the selection was consumed into a mask); Select/Subject (ps_menu 1461, event autoCutout) gives an automatic subject selection. Neither brushes an edge, and app.runMenuItem refuses these numeric menu ids (harvest audit).
use_for: hair and fur cut-outs for portraits, pets and fashion shots
soft or wispy edges such as fluffy fabric or plants against a busy background
cleaning the edge of a Quick Selection or Object Selection before compositing
avoid: hard, geometric edges: a Pen Tool path gives a cleaner result
edges where subject and background share colour: expect halos; paint the mask by hand
outside Select and Mask: the tool is not available there

review.changes: script_api: replaced "open the workspace via runMenuItem(1115)" with the verified refineSelectionEdge event (runs without the workspace) and the autoCutout event for Select/Subject; the harvest audit says runMenuItem refuses these ids.

cards.name: Remove Tool
cards.summary: An AI-assisted healing brush: you paint over an unwanted object and, when the stroke ends, Photoshop fills the area with plausible background, handling larger and more complex removals than the Spot Healing Brush.
cards.how: Pick it from the toolbar (in current Photoshop it sits with the healing tools; the harvest records no group or default shortcut, since it is not in the install's keyboard-shortcut file; the harvested Spot Healing Brush group has an unnamed second member, toolbar key 'caft', which is probably this tool, not confirmed). Set the brush a little larger than the object, paint over the whole object including its shadow, and release; overlapping strokes refine the fill. The harvest read back no tool options; from knowledge, the options bar has brush size, Sample All Layers and Remove after each stroke, and recent releases add generative and Find Distractions options. Those options are not confirmed by this harvest.
cards.script_api: Only the tool can be selected: app.currentTool = "removeTool" (harvest invoke). The closest scripted route is a selection (Selection.select) followed by Edit/Content-Aware Fill (ps_menu 1510) by its harvested event, executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("cafWorkspace"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO), which in the harvest's live test filled the selection onto a new layer without opening the workspace. Edit/Generative Fill (ps_menu 1750) has no script route in this harvest (not run, since it spends generative credits).
use_for: removing tourists, photobombers and passers-by from travel or event photos
erasing power lines, signs and litter from backgrounds
cleaning dust, props and stray objects from product photos
avoid: when the exact source of the fill matters: use the Clone Stamp Tool
near faces, hands and text: it can invent detail; check closely or clone by hand
on an empty layer without Sample All Layers: there are no pixels to fill from

review.changes: script_api: Generative Fill (1750) has no harvested script route, so it is no longer offered as a scripted step; Content-Aware Fill (1510) is given with its verified cafWorkspace event, which ran without opening the workspace. how: pointed to the unnamed 'caft' slot in the harvested Spot Healing group as the probable toolbar home.

cards.name: Rotate View Tool
cards.summary: Rotates the on-screen view of the canvas, like turning a sheet of paper on a desk, without changing any pixels, so you can draw or retouch at a comfortable angle.
cards.how: Press R (it shares the Hand Tool flyout). Drag on the canvas to turn the view; Shift snaps to 15 degree steps. The options bar has a Rotation Angle field (harvest key angle, read back 0), Reset View, and Rotate All Windows (rotateAll, read back false). It needs the GPU drawing mode; Esc or Reset View returns to 0.
cards.script_api: Only the tool can be selected: app.currentTool = "rotateTool" (harvest invoke); the harvest records no call that rotates the view. Rotating the actual image is a different job: Image/Image Rotation/Arbitrary (ps_menu 2994), 90 Clockwise (2991), or Edit/Transform/Rotate (ps_menu 2205) for a layer.
use_for: inking and painting with a tablet at a natural hand angle
retouching along a diagonal edge with comfortable strokes
masking or cleaning edges that run at awkward angles
avoid: when the exported image must be rotated: use Image/Image Rotation or Edit/Transform/Rotate
checking a composition with fresh eyes: View/Flip Horizontal (ps_menu 1284) mirrors the view without touching pixels
